clue.text: Gentle persuasion very much associated with paper by group reportedly

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so kind'
FT is the Financial Times, the paper this puzzle appears in

indicators.note: reportedly says we want a word that sounds like the group word, not its spelling

parts.note: a cell is a small group, as of activists

explanation.surface: A newspaper's sales pitch is gentle, linked to the paper and some group, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: FT is this puzzle's own newspaper, the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-pressure sales approach that coaxes rather than pushes is a mild form of persuasion.

clue.text: With little confidence about a gang extremely unkempt

indicators.note: about says the timid word goes round the rest

parts.note: shy means timid, lacking confidence

indicators.note: extremely takes the outer letters of gang

explanation.surface: A timid person faces a gang of scruffy types.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaggy hair or fur is long and untidy, so it looks messy and uncombed.

clue.text: Religious house's fair reformed line

indicators.note: reformed says the letters of fair are rearranged

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A monastery's fair takes a reformed line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' and 'Religious' together hint at the Reformation, but 'reformed' only rearranges fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A friary is a monastery or convent of friars, a religious community's house.

clue.text: Notice daughter welcoming sailor in ground invariably wet

indicators.note: welcoming means the notice and daughter pieces take the sailor in

parts.note: to see is to notice
AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A daughter spots a sailor on soggy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The bed of the sea is ground that is always under water, a witty description.

clue.text: Language from aunt in hail — shocking!

indicators.note: shocking suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An aunt caught in a hailstorm finds it shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithuanian is the Baltic language spoken in Lithuania.

clue.text: Upper room briefly referring to dress

indicators.note: briefly asks for the word cut short, its last letter dropped

parts.note: an attic is a room at the top of a house
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: An attic gets a brief mention in connection with clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn, especially formal or special garments, is what dress means as a noun.

clue.text: Describing many coins as not to be trusted?

definitions.meaning: coins with heads on one side and tails on the other each have a pair of sides

explanation.definitionFit: Literally having a pair of sides, as a coin; figuratively, hypocritical and deceitful.

clue.text: Some chain there, debt-laden, owing money

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shop chain is heavily indebted and owes money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from accounts where debts were written in red ink, so it means overdrawn.

clue.text: All extremely acceptable among Europeans

indicators.note: among puts the other pieces between the two European letters

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, twice for the plural
very means extremely
on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: All agree it is highly acceptable among Europeans.
explanation.definitionFit: Everybody, every single person, is what 'all' means used as a pronoun.

clue.text: Girl hugs worker in Spanish port

indicators.note: hugs means the girl's name wraps around the worker

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
an ant is the standard crossword worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A girl embraces a labourer in a Spanish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a seaport city on Spain's Costa Blanca.

clue.text: Attempt at Estuary English originally — one hides one's face a bit!

definitions.text: one hides one's face a bit!

parts.note: a go is an attempt, as in 'have a go'

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letters of the following two words

explanation.surface: Trying out an Estuary accent, someone is embarrassed enough to hide their face.
explanation.walkthrough: Estuary English is the accent of London and the Thames estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: A small chin beard covers part of the face, hence the playful, partial-concealment description.

clue.text: Magnificent ravine not half famous

parts.note: a gorge is a deep narrow ravine

indicators.note: not half drops the first half of the six-letter word famous

explanation.surface: A splendid ravine is only partly well known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very', a false trail here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something splendid, beautiful or richly impressive; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Where bloomer is made — banker forgetting New Year?

indicators.note: forgetting says the letter for new is dropped from banker

explanation.surface: A banker who forgets New Year makes a howler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, given the forgetful banker; it is a long crusty loaf with diagonal slashes, a British bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop or workplace where bread such as a bloomer loaf is baked.

clue.text: Time that was painful — intially sullen manner becomes standard

parts.note: ouch is what you say when something hurts

indicators.note: intially (so spelt in the clue) takes the opening letter of sullen

parts.note: tone is manner, as in a tone of voice

explanation.surface: A painful episode turns a sullen attitude into the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion or benchmark against which things are tested, from the stone used to assay gold.

clue.text: Surprise text for translation — passing around warning

indicators.note: passing around says the text goes round the warning

parts.note: an unseen is a passage given to students to translate without preparation
fore is the golfer's shouted warning

explanation.surface: An unexpected passage to translate goes round with a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools an 'unseen' is an exam passage to translate at sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, as in a surprise visit, it means not expected or predicted.

clue.text: Gestures about poor sod's nightwear

indicators.note: about says the gestures go round the rest

parts.note: becks are beckoning gestures

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of sod are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone waves at an unfortunate fellow wearing night clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Socks worn in bed to keep the feet warm are an item of nightwear.

clue.text: Old soldier's revamped rifle is used at beginning

indicators.note: revamped says the letters are refashioned into a new order
at beginning takes the first letter of used

explanation.surface: A veteran's rifle, refurbished, is used from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusilier was originally a soldier armed with a fusil, a light musket.

clue.text: Drug stashed in one pen there

indicators.note: stashed in says the answer is concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Drugs are hidden in a pen over there.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary potion in Homer that banishes grief, so a drug of forgetfulness.

clue.text: High spirits of last couples in Essex club after cancan — nice!

indicators.note: last couples in takes the final two letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: An Essex nightclub after a cancan show: what fun!
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberance is lively, cheerful energy, which is just what high spirits are.

clue.text: Aircraft facility worker failing to finish starts to get angry rollicking

indicators.note: failing to finish drops the final letter of the worker

parts.note: a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

indicators.note: starts to takes the first letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A labourer starts getting angry and gives someone a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rollicking' is British slang for a severe telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A large shed where aircraft are housed and serviced.

clue.text: Girl sadly orphaned or abandoned

indicators.note: sadly suggests the remaining letters are rearranged
abandoned says the word or is dropped from orphaned

explanation.surface: A girl is sadly orphaned or left alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' removes OR from ORPHANED, leaving PHANED, which 'sadly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne is a girl's name, from the nymph of Greek myth turned into a laurel.

clue.text: Condition of charge, covering total, observed only intermittently

indicators.note: covering says the charge goes round the rest

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: observed only intermittently takes alternate letters of total

explanation.surface: The state of a charge covering a total that's seen only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: In fine fettle means in good shape, so the word means state or condition.

clue.text: It might polish quiet home connected with monarch

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
in means at home
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Something that shines quietly links home and the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who polishes shoes or brass, a shoe shiner, is literally one who makes things shine.

clue.text: Adventure, sad, peace transformed

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of sad and peace are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: An adventure turns sadness into peace.
explanation.definitionFit: A daring or mischievous adventure, a romp or caper, is what this word names.

clue.text: Fabric given in couturier's first tip having character after all

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of couturier's

parts.note: a hint is a tip, a piece of advice
Z is the letter that comes after all the others in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A designer offers advice on a cloth that has character.
explanation.definitionFit: Chintz is a glazed printed cotton cloth, often flowery, used for curtains.

clue.text: Has desire, torrid — its chances are remote

parts.note: longs means yearns or has a desire
torrid means very hot

explanation.surface: Someone yearns passionately for something with little hope of success.
explanation.definitionFit: A bet or venture with low odds of success is unlikely, a remote chance.

clue.text: Conceal feature of TV set

definitions.meaning: to hide something from view, as with a partition
the display panel of a television on which the picture appears

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to hide; as a noun it is the display surface of a television.

clue.text: Behind Democrat linked to slip before about island

indicators.note: about says the slip-and-before pair goes round the island letter

parts.note: to err is to slip up
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A Democrat's gaffe before an island trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a preposition, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-borrowed euphemism for the buttocks, the bottom or backside.
